lesson.headline: JLPT N4 (Elementary) — Verb Conjugations & Adjectives
lesson.lead: Progressing from polite styles to basic plain/casual formats. Developing competency in fluid spoken expressions and complex conditional phrases.
bullets: Verb Forms: Plain/Dictionary Form (to eat - たべる), Negative Form (tabenai - たべない), Past Form (tabeta - たべた), and Te-form (tabete - たべた).
The Vital Te-form (~て): Used to link actions, make polite requests (~て ください), and represent ongoing states (~て いる).
Conditional Structures: ~たら (tara - if/when general condition), ~と (to - natural/inevitable consequence, e.g. "when spring comes, flowers bloom").
Adjective Conjugations: I-adjectives (e.g. さむい) vs Na-adjectives (e.g. しずかな). Past negative of さむい is 寒くなかった (samukunakatta).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form to express the potential: "I can speak Japanese." (日本語が___。)
quizzes.explain: Potential verbs in Group 1 are formed by changing the final -u sound to -eru. 話す (to speak) becomes 話せる, and in polite form, 話せます (can speak).

quizzes.q: Choose the correct conditional form for: "If it rains tomorrow, let's stay home." (明日、雨が___たら、家にいましょう。)
quizzes.explain: The conditional form "~たら" (~tara) is created by adding "ra" to the past casual (Ta-form) of a verb. The past casual of 降る (to fall/rain) is 降った, so it is 降ったら.

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence to mean "Please try to study every day": "毎日、勉強する___にしてください。"
quizzes.explain: The pattern "~ようにする" (~youni suru) is used to express making a continuous effort or establishing a habit ("try/make an effort to do X").

quizzes.q: Choose the correct form to express natural consequence: "When spring comes, flowers bloom." (春に___と、花が咲きます。)
quizzes.explain: The conditional particle "と" (to) expresses a natural, automatic, or inevitable consequence. It follows the dictionary form (なる + と).

quizzes.q: Complete the sentence: "I heard that Mr. Tanaka will not go." (田中さんは行かない___です。)
quizzes.explain: To express hearsay ("I heard that..."), use plain form + "そうです" (sou desu). "行かない" is the plain negative form, so "行かないそうです" means "I heard he is not going."

quizzes.q: How do you say "This book seems difficult" (based on appearance)? (この本は___そうです。)
quizzes.explain: To express conjecture or impression ("looks like / seems..."), drop the final "-i" from an I-adjective and add "そうです". 難しい becomes 難しそうです.

〜すぎる (sugiru) means "to do too much".
〜でしょう (deshou) is used for probability or guessing ("probably").

quizzes.explain: 〜てもいいですか (te mo ii desu ka) is used to ask for permission.
〜ておく (te oku) means to do something in advance.
〜てしまう (te shimau) implies regretting an action or finishing it completely.
つもり (tsumori) expresses an intention or plan.
〜ば (ba) is the conditional form ("if it is cheap").

〜ておく (te oku) means to do something in advance.
〜てしまう (te shimau) implies regretting an action or finishing it completely.
つもり (tsumori) expresses an intention or plan.
〜ば (ba) is the conditional form ("if it is cheap").

quizzes.q: 母は明日からダイエットする（　　）にしました。
quizzes.explain: ことにする (koto ni suru) means "to decide to do".
